verdict.summary: TeraWulf is no longer economically just a bitcoin miner: Q2 2026 HPC lease revenue was $31.9 million, 71% of total revenue, and capacity reached 102 MW in early July. The 401 MW, 20-year Anthropic lease carries roughly $19 billion of base contract value, with Google credit support reducing tenant-credit risk. That pivot is real. It is also unfinished and expensive. Q2 revenue was only $44.8 million, non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was negative $18.3 million, another 336 MW was under construction, and management's $8-$10 million cost per IT MW implies billions of future deployment spend. The April base offering priced 47.4 million shares at $19 and included a 7.11 million-share option; the Q2 10-Q proves the option was exercised, bringing completed issuance to 54.51 million shares and $1.0357 billion gross. Converts, project notes and warrants remain material. Cash and restricted cash near $3.0 billion cannot be viewed apart from more than $5 billion of debt. The D grade reflects weak current earnings and dilution. The unchanged $16.29 plan is rejected: $17.4899 and $17.8899 offer only 0.78R and 1.04R against the $14.75 stop.
whyBuy: Q2 HPC lease revenue was $31.9M, 71% of total revenue.
Revenue capacity reached 102 MW in early July.

whyAvoid: TeraWulf posted negative $18.3M of Q2 adjusted EBITDA on a non-GAAP basis.
336 MW under construction at $8M-$10M per IT MW implies heavy remaining capex.
The April deal sold 54.51M shares for $1.0357B gross after the 7.11M-share option was exercised.
Debt exceeded $5B and warrants reserved roughly 80.9M shares in the reviewed disclosures.

business.overview:
TeraWulf operates power-secured campuses that now earn primarily HPC lease revenue, alongside residual bitcoin-mining economics. Revenue depends on billable IT megawatts, contractual rent and, for mining, hash production and bitcoin prices.

The AI channel is direct: TeraWulf develops powered shells and cooling, tenants install or contract compute, and rent starts as capacity is delivered. The 401 MW Anthropic agreement, supported by Google credit, can convert power access into long-duration datacenter cash flow from 2027 onward.

The model breaks if construction misses delivery dates, cost per MW exceeds plan, tenant support weakens or capital markets close before rent starts. Mining exposure adds commodity volatility, while converts, project debt, warrants and recent equity issuance divide future project economics among multiple claims. Investors must therefore compare delivered, billable capacity with construction spending and all equity-linked claims before capitalizing the full lease value into today's common shares.
business.moat: Lake Mariner's low-carbon power access, existing campus infrastructure and a credit-supported anchor lease create a financing and time-to-power advantage. The moat is conditional on delivering 401 MW on budget; a signed lease does not remove construction risk.

earnings.beatNote: Q2 2026 revenue was $44.8M, with $31.9M from HPC leasing, or 71% of the total. Non-GAAP adjusted EBITDA was negative $18.3M. Revenue capacity was 81 MW at June 30 and 102 MW in early July, while 336 MW remained under construction. Management targets 250-500 MW of incremental annual contracting and estimates construction at $8M-$10M per IT MW. TeraWulf supplied contracting and construction targets but no formal consolidated revenue or EBITDA guidance. The caveat is timing: the large Anthropic build begins initial delivery in the second half of 2027 and reaches full delivery in early 2028, leaving a long funding period before rent. No confirmed TeraWulf next-earnings date was listed by the issuer after the source check.

capitalStructure.shareHistory: TeraWulf's pivot has been funded through common equity, converts, warrants and project debt. The April final 424B5 priced 47.4M shares at $19 and described a 7.11M-share option; the Q2 10-Q proves that 54.51M shares were ultimately issued for $1.0357B gross, so the option was exercised and must be included. Preliminary prospectuses are the same program, not extra issuance. Against roughly 499.0M basic shares, initial conversion rates imply about 190.8M gross convertible shares across the 2030, 2031 and 2032 notes, and approximately 73.6M Google warrants are additional claims. The resulting 763.4M minimum observable basic-plus-quantified-claims sensitivity excludes other warrants and awards and is not a fully diluted forecast. Capped calls may reduce economic dilution but do not reduce the legal claims; project notes remain debt and restricted construction cash is not excess parent liquidity.

filings.finding: The June Form 10-Q reports TeraWulf's quarterly balance sheet, operating capacity, debt and warrant exposure and proves completion of 54.51M April offering shares for $1.0357B gross, including exercise of the 7.11M-share option.
The 2025 Form 10-K establishes the annual mining, infrastructure, controls and capital baseline; it predates the April common offering and the later Anthropic lease economics.
The August earnings Form 8-K furnishes Q2 revenue of $44.8M and the HPC leasing update through exhibits; it is a current report, not an equity issuance filing.

The final April 424B5 prices 47.4M common shares at $19 for $900.6M gross, states expected delivery and describes a 7.11M-share option. The later Q2 10-Q proves 54.51M shares and $1.0357B gross, confirming exercise of that option.
This April 424B5 contains offering terms preceding final completion; use it for security mechanics, not as an additional share sale on top of the definitive completed offering.

This preliminary 424B5 launched the common offering and described proposed terms; it does not support double-counting proceeds or shares later finalized in accession 0001104659-26-044031. This classification controls the editorial conclusion.

The April S-3ASR establishes automatic shelf capacity used for the common offering; it is not execution proof. The final terms and later Q2 10-Q together establish 54.51M completed shares for $1.0357B gross.

contrarianRisks: The April common offering was completed issuance, unlike generic shelf capacity.
Warrants reserve approximately 80.9M shares and are a real potential overhang.
Convertible debt and project notes have different recourse and dilution mechanics.
Restricted cash is tied to financing structures and is not all deployable at parent level.
The $19B Anthropic base value depends on multi-year delivery, not immediate revenue recognition.

macro.impact: TeraWulf monetizes power twice: directly through bitcoin mining and increasingly through AI leases.
